text: The Sun is the most powerful thing in our sky.
Take one cubic metre from the very centre of its core.
asr: Take one cubic meter from the very center of its core.

text: It puts out about as much heat as... a compost heap.
Your body makes more heat per cubic metre than that. Several times more.
asr: Your body makes more heat per cubic meter than that. Several times more.

text: Congratulations. You are out-performing a star. Please don't put it on your CV.
asr: Congratulations. You are outperforming a star. Please don't put it on your CV.

text: So how does a compost heap light up the solar system? It's just... very, very big.
The light warming your face today was made in the core thousands of years ago.
It spent all that time bumping around inside, then crossed to Earth in eight minutes, like it suddenly remembered it had somewhere to be.
Even fusion is a struggle. Protons push each other away. By normal physics, they should basically never touch.
They only fuse thanks to quantum tunnelling. Which is physics for: walking through the wall anyway.
asr: They only fuse thanks to quantum tunneling. Which is physics for walking through the wall anyway.

text: Even then, the average proton waits about nine billion years for its turn.
asr: Even then, the average proton weights about 9 billion years for its turn.

text: Here's the twist. If fusion were easy, the Sun would have burned out long before anything crawled out of the sea.
Instead, it took its time. Long enough for oceans... dinosaurs... and you.
So the next time someone calls you lazy, just tell them you're pacing yourself. Like a star.
